title: Notable biology and biomedical papers — arXiv batch of 9 November 2026
candidate_pool_scope: 20 entries in the q-bio combined recent listing plus 5 new submissions in physics.med-ph; standalone cs.BI listing could not be independently confirmed.
global_caveat: arXiv has no official trending chart; this inferred relevance-and-evidence ranking is not a popularity ranking, and arXiv covers only part of biomedical preprinting, with much clinical and experimental work appearing on bioRxiv or medRxiv.

sections.title: Headline
sections.summary: Daily snapshot 2026-11-10T01:25:17Z; latest batch Monday 2026-11-09. Thirteen notable papers led by multimodal genomics, large-scale biomedical data, and medical imaging. This is a relevance-and-evidence ranking, not a popularity chart; arXiv biomedical coverage is incomplete.

sections.title: Synchronized Optimal Transport Reconstructs Coupled Transcriptomic and Chromatin Dynamics
sections.abstract: COATI models RNA and ATAC developmental trajectories in separate spaces and is evaluated on synthetic data and four developmental datasets, including held-out-stage reconstruction.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors say synchronized unbalanced optimal transport improves held-out population reconstruction and preserves chromatin heterogeneity and developmental lineage relationships.
sections.unique_caveat: Trajectories are inferred from destructive snapshots, not tracked individual cells; results depend on a pretrained RNA-to-ATAC map and do not establish true lineage paths.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four developmental datasets, held-out-stage tests, and agreement of inferred lineage responses with independent CRISPR perturbation and epigenetic results.

sections.title: Health-System-Wide Mapping of Demographic Information in Routine Clinical Histopathology
sections.abstract: An analysis of 1.3 million H&E slides from 257,322 patients across 25 organs found that models could recover sex, age group, and self-reported race from histology, with performance varying by organ and label.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors provide a systematic map of demographic-associated information in routine histopathology and identify possible implications for shortcut learning; explanations for the signals remain hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: Predictability does not identify its biological or social source. This is a retrospective single-health-system analysis; diagnosis grouping is not external replication or causal evidence.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Large retrospective cohort spanning 1.3 million slides, 257,322 patients, 25 organs, and 69 organ-demographic combinations.

sections.title: Personalized health coaching via coachable health age and counterfactual wearable trajectories
sections.abstract: A wearable-derived health-age metric and a model trained on over 2.2 million person-weeks forecast responses to lifestyle changes and generate counterfactual coaching plans, evaluated across three cohorts and by expert reviewers.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors report improved prognostic discrimination over age, sex, and BMI, multi-week response forecasts, and higher expert preference for counterfactual-grounded plans.
sections.unique_caveat: Forecast accuracy and expert review do not show that plans change behavior or health outcomes; the abstract reports no prospective intervention.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cohorts of 2,780, 22,748, and 1,464 participants; about 100,000-person SensorWM pretraining set; blinded coach and clinician review.

sections.title: Navigating Selection Bias in Genome-wide Association Studies (GWAS)
sections.abstract: A methods review organizes ten ways to diagnose or correct GWAS selection bias by available data and selection mechanism, with R implementations for nine methods and simulated examples.
sections.claimed_contribution: The review offers a decision framework for participation, case-control, index-event, sex-differential, and survival-related selection bias.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a methods synthesis, not new population-scale validation; every correction remains conditional on its assumptions and required data.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Ten methods compared with assumptions and data needs, companion code, and worked simulations.

sections.title: Dual-energy cardiac DSA imaging using a dual-layer flat-panel detector: in vivo validation study
sections.abstract: A dual-energy material-decomposition method using a dual-layer detector is evaluated with simulations and preliminary in-vivo swine cardiac angiography; the authors report improved vessel contrast and reduced scatter effects.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors propose temporally subtracted low/high-energy projections with penalized-likelihood decomposition to improve cardiac vessel visualization without requiring precise scatter correction.
sections.unique_caveat: Preliminary animal validation is not human clinical evidence; broader motion and multi-material performance remain to be tested.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Monte Carlo simulations and in-vivo swine experiments on a clinical DSA system; authors report over 80% lower scatter impact in simulation.

sections.title: KineCouple: Substrate-conditioned residual readout for enzyme kinetic prediction
sections.abstract: KineCouple uses substrate-conditioned cross-attention over residue features to predict enzyme kcat and Km, reporting small pooled out-of-fold improvements over reproduced CataPro results.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors condition residue-level aggregation on substrate features while keeping ProtT5 and MolT5 encoders frozen.
sections.unique_caveat: Metric gains are small; repeated-run variability and matched controls are needed, and attention weights do not establish physical catalytic contacts.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct enzyme-kinetics benchmark; reported kcat RMSE/PCC changes 1.333/0.492 to 1.330/0.496 and Km 0.998/0.633 to 0.997/0.634.

sections.title: Smart Spectral Doppler Ultrasound Imaging using Motion Tracking based on Wide-beam transmission and Neural Networks: Preliminary Results
sections.abstract: A single-transmit wide-beam Doppler method tracks vessel motion and updates the sample volume; simulations and in-vivo carotid-artery and hepatic-vein demonstrations report improved spectral signal-to-noise under tissue motion.
sections.claimed_contribution: Wide-beam transmission aims to preserve pulse-repetition frequency while a lightweight tracker follows motion and repositions the Doppler sample volume.
sections.unique_caveat: In-vivo evidence is limited to two demonstrations; performance across patients, pathologies, and routine clinical workflows is not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Field II simulations plus in-vivo demonstrations in two vessels; reported spectral-SNR gains of 9.3 dB and 4.5 dB.

sections.title: SmartBloch-Agent: An Agentic Framework for Automated MRI Sequence Design and Optimization
sections.abstract: SmartBloch-Agent uses an AI agent and an in-house Bloch simulator to turn natural-language imaging objectives into MRI sequence designs, simulations, reconstructions, and optimization feedback.
sections.claimed_contribution: The framework links sequence construction, physical simulation, parameter search, reconstruction, and evaluation into an agent-driven research loop.
sections.unique_caveat: Reported evidence is computational; scanner deployment and independent validation on acquired patient data are not established.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Cross-listed in medical physics, AI, and imaging; authors report automated experiments across varied objectives and improved parameter-estimation and quantitative-reconstruction metrics.

sections.title: Pangenome Peeling: Decomposing Weighted Adjacencies into Path-Forest Genomes
sections.abstract: The authors define an inverse pangenome problem that reconstructs constituent linear genomes from weighted adjacency graphs and compare two algorithms on simulated data.
sections.claimed_contribution: The maximum-spanning-tree path decomposition reportedly recovers simulated constituent genomes more faithfully than sequential edge addition as genome size grows.
sections.unique_caveat: Evaluation is simulation-based; performance on real, noisy pangenome graphs and ancestral genomes remains unshown.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct genomics application, formal problem definition and lower-bound result, and simulation comparison using genome similarity and matching criteria.

sections.title: Protein B-factor modeling with local magnitude
sections.abstract: A local geometric descriptor for protein structures modestly improves B-factor prediction across protein benchmarks while reducing feature-extraction cost for large structures.
sections.claimed_contribution: Nearest-neighbor local magnitude features preserve residue-level structural information and have lower asymptotic factorization cost than global magnitude for large structures.
sections.unique_caveat: Predictive gains are modest and experiments use a single-seed configuration; faster extraction is not universal for small proteins.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: 364 proteins in fitting analyses and 345 in blind prediction across three validation protocols; local-feature gains are consistent but small.

sections.title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Annealing for Protein Side-Chain Optimization: A Feasibility Study
sections.abstract: A hybrid annealer is compared with Gurobi on 40 side-chain optimization instances derived from 20 experimentally determined protein structures; the authors report competitive or lower-energy solutions on larger instances.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that side-chain optimization is a suitable binary-quadratic problem for testing hybrid annealing and report reaching certified optima when available.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a feasibility study, not experimental protein-design validation; comparisons with heuristics tailored to side-chain optimization are still needed.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Forty instances from 20 structures and comparisons with a commercial solver at multiple runtime budgets.

sections.title: Medical Radioisotopes: Clinical Demand, Production Physics, and Untapped Pathways
sections.abstract: A review maps more than 40 medical radioisotopes across established, underused, and emerging groups, connecting clinical applications with production routes and radiochemical constraints.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors identify production-side bottlenecks and underused isotopes that could merit further assessment for clinical access.
sections.unique_caveat: This is a review, not a trial or new evidence that expanding production changes patient outcomes.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Broad cross-disciplinary review of clinical demand and production constraints across 40+ isotopes; included for direct medical-physics relevance, not popularity.

sections.title: Medical Radioisotopes: Supply-chain Resilience, Distributed Production, and Access
sections.abstract: A review pairs literature analysis with expert interviews to assess isotope supply disruptions and argues for regional accelerator centers alongside centralized reactor production.
sections.claimed_contribution: The authors argue that regional accelerator production could complement aging centralized reactors and reduce single-point and cross-border vulnerabilities.
sections.unique_caveat: The proposal is a literature- and interview-based analysis; the effects of regional centers on access and patient outcomes are not evaluated.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Direct relevance to nuclear-medicine isotope access; authors combine 2025–2026 supply-chain cases with expert interviews.

sections.title: Trending Research Themes
sections.summary: Selected papers combine multimodal and population-level inference; computational protein biology; and translational imaging/infrastructure work. Evidence spans cohort analyses, models, animal imaging, simulation, reviews, and interviews; these are separate evidence types rather than a field-wide shift.

sections.title: Open Problems and Research Directions
sections.summary: Follow-up directions include external blinded pathology replication; direct lineage-tracing and sensitivity tests for COATI; repeated-seed and matched-compute protein benchmarks; noisy real-graph testing for pangenome reconstruction; broader imaging validation; prospective wearable-coaching evaluation; real-scanner MRI testing; and outcome/access analyses for isotope-production proposals.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.summary: The strongest papers pair computational methods with broad cohorts, multiple developmental datasets, or explicit animal/in-vivo imaging tests. Others are reviews or simulations. Attention evidence is too sparse for a popularity ranking, and none of these preprints alone supports a change in clinical practice.
